text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS
-- The forint's monthly crawling peg devaluation rate will drop from 1.1 percent to one percent on August 15, Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy announced yesterday.

-- The Parliament passed a long-awaited advertising bill Tuesday with 198 votes for, 60 against and 23 abstentions. The law forbids advertisemnets that violate personal rights, religious feelings, public morality or public taste or abuse personal data, and outlaws advertisements disguised as news.
-- The Parliament on Tuesday ratified the treaty on altering the national border as a result of regulating the water management of the Ipoly, Sajo and Ronyva rivesr between Hungary and Slovakia.
-- Interior Minister Gabor Luncze said on Tuesday that the electoral law would only be amended with the agreement of a majority of political forces following seven-party consultations.

-- The Supreme Court struck down on Pest county resolutions of the opposition Christian Democrat's party on the lection of party officials, but the court decision will not affect the re-election of Gyorgy Giczy as party president last weeke-end.
-- Prime Minister Gyula Horn will lead a delegation to Amsterdam today, to get informed on the results of the European Union's intergovernmental conference that ended on June 18.
-- The London-based credit rating agency IBCA upgraded Hungary's long-term foreign debt to BBB from BBB-minus.
-- The National Bank of Hungary announced a cut in the central bank base rate to an annual 21 percent from 21.5 percent, effective July 1.
-- Postabank agreed with its shareholders on a capital increase on Tuesday, but deputy CEO Robert Muranyi said the results will not be made public until after Thursday's board meeting.
MAGYAR NEMZET

-- President Arpad Goncz met former U.S. Secretary of State Henry Kissinger and Souty nKorean President Kim Young-Sam in New York where he is attending the United Nation's conference on the environment.
NEPSZABADSAG

-- Russia offers MiG-29 fighters for sale and is ready to upgrade the MiG-21s owned by thye Hungarian air forces, a delegation of the Russian Duma's defense committee, visiting the Parliaments' defense committee, said.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
-- The latest data from the Central Statistical Office shows a continuing economic boom in Hungary.
NAPI GAZDASAG
-- The cabinet is expected to agree on a draft 1998 central budget at its Thursday meeting.
